question.:question/problem: Given that $f(x) = x^{-2/3}$ and that $F^{′}(x) = f(x)$, calculate $F(x)$. Assume $x>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that integration is the opposite of differentiation. So, if ${F}^{'}(x)=f(x),$ then integrating both sides of this equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{'}(x) & =f(x) \\ \int {F}^{'}(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ F(x) & =\int f(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can use the power rule with $n=-\frac{2}{3}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x) & =\int f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ & =\int x^{-2/3}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{x^{-2/3+1}}{(-\frac{2}{3}+1)}+C \\ & =3x^{1/3}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $\frac{1}{\sqrt[7]{{x}^{13}}}=\frac{1}{{x}^{13/7}}={x}^{-13/7}.$ So, we can use the power rule with $n=-\frac{13}{7}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt[7]{{x}^{13}}}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{-13/7}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-13/7+1}}{-\frac{13}{7}+1}+C \\  & =-\frac{7}{6}{x}^{-6/7}+C \\  & =-\frac{7}{6{x}^{6/7}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Calculate the integral of $\frac{1}{\sqrt[7]{{x}^{15}}}$. Assume $x>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Note that $\frac{1}{\sqrt[7]{{x}^{15}}}=\frac{1}{{x}^{15/7}}={x}^{-15/7}.$ So, we can use the power rule with $n=-\frac{15}{7}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt[7]{{x}^{15}}}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{-15/7}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-15/7+1}}{-\frac{15}{7}+1}+C \\  & =-\frac{7}{8}{x}^{-8/7}+C \\  & =-\frac{7}{8{x}^{8/7}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
